claim: In electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM), the electron beam used for imaging causes the sample to move.
source: In electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM), the electron beam that is used for imaging also causes the sample to move.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the abstract and is supported by multiple citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Beam-induced motion blurs cryo-EM images and limits the resolution attainable by single-particle analysis.
source: This motion blurs the images and limits the resolution attainable by single-particle analysis.
evidence: This is stated as a known consequence of beam-induced motion, supported by established understanding in the field.

claim: Correcting for beam-induced motion by processing movies from fast direct-electron detectors allowed structure determination to near-atomic resolution from 35,000 ribosome particles.
source: In a previous Research article (Bai et al., 2013) we showed that correcting for this motion by processing movies from fast direct-electron detectors allowed structure determination to near-atomic resolution from 35,000 ribosome particles.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous publication by the authors.

claim: The new movie processing algorithm is applicable to a much wider range of specimens than the previous algorithm.
source: In this Research advance article, we show that an improved movie processing algorithm is applicable to a much wider range of specimens.
evidence: This is demonstrated through application to four different data sets of varying particle sizes in the manuscript.

claim: The new algorithm estimates straight movement tracks by considering multiple particles that are close to each other in the field of view.
source: The new algorithm estimates straight movement tracks by considering multiple particles that are close to each other in the field of view, and models the fall-off of high-resolution information content by radiation damage in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach taken in the new algorithm.

claim: The new algorithm models the fall-off of high-resolution information content by radiation damage in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The new algorithm estimates straight movement tracks by considering multiple particles that are close to each other in the field of view, and models the fall-off of high-resolution information content by radiation damage in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach and is demonstrated through the relative B-factor analysis in the results.

claim: The new algorithm has potential for significantly improving cryo-EM structures for particles smaller than 200 kDa.
source: Application of the new algorithm to four data sets illustrates its potential for significantly improving cryo-EM structures, even for particles that are smaller than 200 kDa.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the γ-secretase example (170 kDa) showing improvement from 4.9 Å to 4.5 Å resolution.

claim: Direct-electron detectors yield higher signal-to-noise ratios than conventional detection devices.
source: The new detectors yield higher signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) than conventional detection devices (McMullan et al., 2009), and are fast enough to record multiple images, that is movies, during typical exposure times.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to McMullan et al., 2009.

claim: Direct-electron detectors are fast enough to record multiple images (movies) during typical exposure times.
source: The new detectors yield higher signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) than conventional detection devices (McMullan et al., 2009), and are fast enough to record multiple images, that is movies, during typical exposure times.
evidence: This is stated as a known capability of direct-electron detectors.

claim: Sample movements in cryo-EM are caused by interactions with the incoming electron beam.
source: The latter allows correction for sample movements that are caused by interactions with the incoming electron beam (Brilot et al., 2012; Campbell et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brilot et al., 2012 and Campbell et al., 2012.

claim: A previous algorithm for beam-induced movement correction of individual ribosome particles allowed calculation of a reconstruction with detail down to 4 Å resolution from only 35,000 asymmetric ribosome particles.
source: Last year, we reported an algorithm for beam-induced movement correction of individual ribosome particles, which allowed us to calculate a reconstruction with a level of detail down to 4 Å resolution from only 35,000 (asymmetric) ribosome particles (Bai et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Li et al. (2013) reported an algorithm to correct for the movement of much larger fields of views, which was used to calculate a 3.3 Å map for the 20S proteasome from 1.8 million asymmetric units.
source: Around the same time, Li et al. (2013) reported an algorithm to correct for the movement of much larger fields of views, which they used to calculate a 3.3 Å map for the 20S proteasome from 1.8 million asymmetric units.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Li et al., 2013.

claim: Movie processing techniques were used to calculate a 3.2 Å map for the large subunit of the yeast mitochondrial ribosomal subunit.
source: More recently, these techniques were also used to calculate a 3.2 Å map for the large subunit of the yeast mitochondrial ribosomal subunit (Amunts et al., 2014), a 3.4 Å structure of the F420-reducing [NiFe] hydrogenase (Allegretti et al., 2014), and a 3.4 Å structure of the TRPV1 ion channel (Liao et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Amunts et al., 2014.

claim: Movie processing techniques were used to calculate a 3.4 Å structure of the F420-reducing [NiFe] hydrogenase.
source: More recently, these techniques were also used to calculate a 3.2 Å map for the large subunit of the yeast mitochondrial ribosomal subunit (Amunts et al., 2014), a 3.4 Å structure of the F420-reducing [NiFe] hydrogenase (Allegretti et al., 2014), and a 3.4 Å structure of the TRPV1 ion channel (Liao et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Allegretti et al., 2014.

claim: Movie processing techniques were used to calculate a 3.4 Å structure of the TRPV1 ion channel.
source: More recently, these techniques were also used to calculate a 3.2 Å map for the large subunit of the yeast mitochondrial ribosomal subunit (Amunts et al., 2014), a 3.4 Å structure of the F420-reducing [NiFe] hydrogenase (Allegretti et al., 2014), and a 3.4 Å structure of the TRPV1 ion channel (Liao et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Liao et al., 2013.

claim: The original beam-induced movement correction algorithm followed particle movement by determining the relative rotations and translations of individual particles in running averages of several movie frames with respect to a common reference map.
source: The original algorithm followed particle movement by determining the relative rotations and translations of individual particles in running averages of several movie frames with respect to a common reference map.
evidence: This is a description of the methodology of the previous algorithm.

claim: The original algorithm does not work well for particles that are much smaller than ribosomes because too low SNRs in the movie frames prohibit accurate orientation determination.
source: However, this approach does not work well for particles that are much smaller than ribosomes, because too low SNRs in the movie frames prohibit accurate orientation determination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations observed when applying the original algorithm to smaller particles.

claim: The approach by Li et al. (2013) suffers less from lower SNRs in smaller particles because each field of view contains many of them.
source: Although the approach by Li et al. (2013) suffers less from lower SNRs in smaller particles (because each field of view contains many of them), it is less suited to model the complicated movement patterns that we and others have observed (Glaeser and Hall, 2011; Brilot et al., 2012; Bai et al., 2013) (also see Figure 1).
evidence: This is an inference about the characteristics of the Li et al. algorithm based on its methodology.

claim: The approach by Li et al. (2013) is less suited to model complicated movement patterns observed in cryo-EM.
source: Although the approach by Li et al. (2013) suffers less from lower SNRs in smaller particles (because each field of view contains many of them), it is less suited to model the complicated movement patterns that we and others have observed (Glaeser and Hall, 2011; Brilot et al., 2012; Bai et al., 2013) (also see Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous observations and by Figure 1 showing complex movement patterns.

claim: Low frequencies in cryo-EM data survive higher electron doses than high frequencies.
source: In addition, neither of the two algorithms accounts for the observation that low frequencies in the data survive higher electron doses than the high frequencies (Unwin and Henderson, 1975; Hayward and Glaeser, 1979; Stark et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Unwin and Henderson, 1975; Hayward and Glaeser, 1979; Stark et al., 1996.

claim: The new approach deals with relatively small particles by considering the movements of multiple particles together.
source: The approach presented here addresses both issues: it deals with relatively small particles by considering the movements of multiple particles together, yet is still able to model complex movement patterns, and it formulates a resolution-dependent radiation damage model.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach taken in the new algorithm.

claim: The new approach is able to model complex movement patterns.
source: The approach presented here addresses both issues: it deals with relatively small particles by considering the movements of multiple particles together, yet is still able to model complex movement patterns, and it formulates a resolution-dependent radiation damage model.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the fitted linear tracks shown in Figure 1 for various complex movement patterns.

claim: The new approach formulates a resolution-dependent radiation damage model.
source: The approach presented here addresses both issues: it deals with relatively small particles by considering the movements of multiple particles together, yet is still able to model complex movement patterns, and it formulates a resolution-dependent radiation damage model.
evidence: This is described in the methodology and demonstrated through the relative B-factor analysis in Figure 2.

claim: Beam-induced rotations for ribosome particles were observed to be only a few degrees.
source: In our previous contribution (Bai et al., 2013), we observed beam-induced rotations for ribosome particles of only a few degrees, which is comparable to the accuracy with which orientations of the individual particles could be determined.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The observed beam-induced rotations for ribosome particles are comparable to the accuracy with which orientations of individual particles could be determined.
source: In our previous contribution (Bai et al., 2013), we observed beam-induced rotations for ribosome particles of only a few degrees, which is comparable to the accuracy with which orientations of the individual particles could be determined.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of rotation magnitudes to orientation determination accuracy.

claim: The observation of small beam-induced rotations agreed with previous observations by Campbell et al. (2012).
source: This agreed with previous observations by others (Campbell et al., 2012), and prompted us to investigate a beam-induced movement correction algorithm that only considers particle translations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Campbell et al., 2012.

claim: The new beam-induced movement correction algorithm only considers particle translations.
source: This agreed with previous observations by others (Campbell et al., 2012), and prompted us to investigate a beam-induced movement correction algorithm that only considers particle translations.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach taken in the new algorithm.

claim: The new approach builds on the original approach where running averages of several movie frames of individual particles are translationally aligned against a common reference.
source: The new approach builds on the original one, where running averages of several movie frames of individual particles are (only translationally) aligned against a common reference.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological foundation of the new algorithm.

claim: For small particles, the translations from individual particle alignments become noisy.
source: Because for small particles these translations become noisy, the new approach fits straight tracks through them, and includes all neighbouring particles on the same field of view in these weighted least-squares fits.
evidence: This is an observation that motivated the development of the new approach, as shown in Figure 1.

claim: The new approach fits straight tracks through particle translations and includes all neighbouring particles on the same field of view in weighted least-squares fits.
source: Because for small particles these translations become noisy, the new approach fits straight tracks through them, and includes all neighbouring particles on the same field of view in these weighted least-squares fits.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach taken in the new algorithm.

claim: The user controls the standard deviation σNB of the Gaussian function that defines the weights for neighbouring particles.
source: The user controls the standard deviation σNB of the Gaussian function that defines all wp′.
evidence: This is a description of a user-controllable parameter in the algorithm.

claim: Smaller values for σNB result in fewer neighbouring particles effectively contributing to the linear fits.
source: Smaller values for σNB result in fewer neighbouring particles effectively contributing to the linear fits, so that less noise may be removed, but more complicated movement patterns may be described.
evidence: This is an inference about the effect of the σNB parameter on the algorithm's behavior.

claim: In cases where beam-induced motions may not be modelled by straight tracks, the method will not yield good results.
source: In cases where the beam-induced motions may not be modelled by straight tracks, for example for bent or zig-zag tracks, this method will not yield good results.
evidence: This is a speculation about the limitations of the method based on its assumptions.

claim: A hybrid approach may be useful to correct for large, possibly non-straight movements using the algorithm by Li et al. (2013) and correct for finer movements using the new algorithm.
source: In such cases, a hybrid approach, as also used for the γ-secretase example below, may be useful to correct for large, possibly non-straight movements using the algorithm by Li et al. (2013) and correct for finer movements using the one described here.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the γ-secretase example in the manuscript.

claim: The fall-off of information content with frequency in cryo-EM data is often modelled by a Gaussian using a B-factor, in analogy to the temperature factor in X-ray crystallography.
source: The fall-off of information content with frequency in cryo-EM data is often modelled by a Gaussian using a B-factor, in analogy to the temperature factor in X-ray crystallography (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003.

claim: The new movie processing approach exploits a B-factor model to describe the dose-dependent signal fall-off throughout the recorded movies by estimating a relative B-factor for each movie frame.
source: The new movie processing approach exploits a similar model to describe the dose-dependent signal fall-off throughout the recorded movies by estimating a (relative) B-factor for each movie frame.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach and is demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: The most common procedure to estimate B-factors in cryo-EM structure determination only works for reconstructions where the signal extends beyond ν = 1/10 Å−1.
source: The most common procedure to estimate B-factors in cryo-EM structure determination, by analyzing the Guinier plot of the logarithm of the amplitudes (τ) of a reconstruction versus the square of the frequency (ν2 = 1/δ2), only works for reconstructions where the signal extends beyond ν = 1/10 Å−1 (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003.

claim: Reconstructions from individual movie frames often do not reach ν = 1/10 Å−1 resolution.
source: Because reconstructions from individual movie frames often do not reach that resolution, an alternative analysis was devised.
evidence: This is an observation that motivated the development of the alternative B-factor estimation approach.

claim: The alternative approach estimates 'relative B-factors' that describe how much faster or slower the signal in reconstructions from individual frames drops with frequency compared to the average reconstruction from all movie frames.
source: Instead of estimating absolute B-factors for each movie frame, the alternative approach merely estimates 'relative B-factors' that describe how much faster (or slower) the signal in reconstructions from individual frames drops with frequency compared to the average reconstruction from all movie frames.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological approach taken in the new algorithm.

claim: If the signal in a reconstruction from a single movie frame drops faster than the signal in a reconstruction from all movie frames, then the relative B-factor will be negative.
source: If the signal in a reconstruction from a single movie frame of all particles drops faster than the signal in a reconstruction from all movie frames, then the relative B-factor will be negative; if the signal in the single-frame reconstruction drops slower, the relative B-factor will be positive.
evidence: This is a definition of how relative B-factors are interpreted in the algorithm.

claim: If the signal in a single-frame reconstruction drops slower than the average reconstruction, the relative B-factor will be positive.
source: If the signal in a reconstruction from a single movie frame of all particles drops faster than the signal in a reconstruction from all movie frames, then the relative B-factor will be negative; if the signal in the single-frame reconstruction drops slower, the relative B-factor will be positive.
evidence: This is a definition of how relative B-factors are interpreted in the algorithm.

claim: Useful frequencies for fitting straight lines in relative Guinier plots were observed from approximately 1/20 Å−1 to the frequency where FSCf = 0.143.
source: In these plots, useful frequencies for fitting straight lines were observed from approximately 1/20 Å−1 to the frequency where FSCf = 0.143.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis performed in the study.

claim: Out-of-plane rotations are not considered in the new approach.
source: Finally, because out-of-plane rotations are not considered in the new approach, one may apply the in-plane translations from the fitted tracks for all movie frames of each particle, and then sum the movie frames using the frequency-dependent weights described above.
evidence: This is a description of a limitation of the methodological approach.

claim: The new approach creates a set of 'polished' average particles with increased SNRs.
source: This creates a set of new 'polished' average particles with increased SNRs, which may again be used in subsequent 2D or 3D classifications or refinements.
evidence: This is a description of the output of the algorithm, with increased SNR demonstrated through improved resolution in Table 1.

claim: The re-weighting of movie frames does not comprise an overall sharpening or dampening of the data.
source: Therefore, the re-weighting of the movie frames thus does not comprise an overall sharpening or dampening of the data, and the estimation of an overall absolute B-factor (as in the last row of Table 1) remains relevant.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mathematical properties of the weighting scheme.

claim: The new approach was tested on four previously published cryo-EM data sets on particles of varying size: human γ-secretase, E. coli β-galactosidase, bovine complex-I, and the large sub-unit of the yeast mitochondrial ribosome.
source: The new approach was tested on four previously published cryo-EM data sets on particles of varying size: human γ-secretase (Lu et al., 2014), Escherichia coli β-galactosidase (Scheres and Chen, 2012; Chen et al., 2013; Vinothkumar et al., 2014a), bovine complex-I (Vinothkumar et al., 2014b), and the large sub-unit (LSU) of the yeast mitochondrial ribosome (Amunts et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design, with citations to the original data sources.

claim: The γ-secretase data set was recorded on a Gatan K2-Summit detector.
source: The data set on the γ-secretase complex was recorded on a Gatan K2-Summit detector; all other data sets were recorded on an FEI Falcon-II detector.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup, also shown in Table 1.

claim: All data sets except γ-secretase were recorded on an FEI Falcon-II detector.
source: The data set on the γ-secretase complex was recorded on a Gatan K2-Summit detector; all other data sets were recorded on an FEI Falcon-II detector.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup, also shown in Table 1.

claim: The K2 detector aims to count single-electron events and has to be used at a much lower dose rate than the Falcon-II.
source: Because the K2 detector aims to count single-electron events, it has to be used at a much lower dose rate than the Falcon-II, which integrates charge during the exposure.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the different operating principles of the two detectors.

claim: The Falcon-II detector integrates charge during the exposure.
source: Because the K2 detector aims to count single-electron events, it has to be used at a much lower dose rate than the Falcon-II, which integrates charge during the exposure.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the detector's operating principle.

claim: The γ-secretase data were recorded using relatively long exposures of 15 s.
source: Consequently, the γ-secretase data were recorded using relatively long exposures of 15 s.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup, also shown in Table 1.

claim: The γ-secretase fields of view were first subjected to the algorithm by Li et al. (2013) to correct for linear drift, and then to the particle-based correction.
source: To correct for linear drift during this time, the recorded fields of view were first subjected to the algorithm by Li et al. (2013), and then to the particle-based correction described here.
evidence: This is a description of the hybrid approach used for the γ-secretase data.

claim: A similar hybrid strategy was applied to F420-reducing [NiFe] hydrogenase using the original movie processing approach.
source: A similar hybrid strategy, but using the original movie processing approach, was also applied to F420-reducing [NiFe] hydrogenase (Allegretti et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Allegretti et al., 2014.

claim: The β-galactosidase, complex-I, and mitoribosome data sets were recorded with exposures of 1–2 s.
source: The other three data sets were recorded with exposures of 1–2 s, and only particle-based movement correction was performed.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup, also shown in Table 1.

claim: Only particle-based movement correction was performed for the β-galactosidase, complex-I, and mitoribosome data sets.
source: The other three data sets were recorded with exposures of 1–2 s, and only particle-based movement correction was performed.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing approach used.

claim: The original movie processing algorithm does not improve resolution for particles smaller than 500 kDa.
source: Whereas the original movie processing algorithm does not improve resolution for particles smaller than 500 kDa, the new approach yields significant improvements for all four cases.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the results in Table 1 showing no improvement or worsening for smaller particles with the original algorithm.

claim: The new approach yields significant improvements for all four test cases.
source: Whereas the original movie processing algorithm does not improve resolution for particles smaller than 500 kDa, the new approach yields significant improvements for all four cases.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the results in Table 1 showing resolution improvements for all four data sets.

claim: The movement tracks after application of the original movie processing algorithm become increasingly noisy for smaller particles.
source: The movement tracks after application of the original movie processing algorithm (but omitting rotational searches) become increasingly noisy for smaller particles, whereas for the mitoribosomes the assumption of linear movements appears to be reasonable.
evidence: This is demonstrated visually in Figure 1 showing the blue tracks.

claim: For mitoribosomes, the assumption of linear movements appears to be reasonable.
source: The movement tracks after application of the original movie processing algorithm (but omitting rotational searches) become increasingly noisy for smaller particles, whereas for the mitoribosomes the assumption of linear movements appears to be reasonable.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of the movement tracks in Figure 1.

claim: All four samples exhibit complex movement patterns that could not be described as a single correlated movement.
source: All four samples exhibit complex movement patterns that could not be described as a single correlated movement, but which are captured by the fitted linear tracks.
evidence: This is demonstrated visually in Figure 1 showing varied movement directions across each field of view.

claim: The complex movement patterns are captured by the fitted linear tracks.
source: All four samples exhibit complex movement patterns that could not be described as a single correlated movement, but which are captured by the fitted linear tracks.
evidence: This is demonstrated visually in Figure 1 showing the white fitted tracks.

claim: For large particles such as ribosomes, a running average that accumulates approximately 5 electrons/Å2 is often a good choice.
source: For large particles such as ribosomes, a running average that accumulates approximately 5 electrons/Å2 (five frames in the example below) is often a good choice.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the experience gained from applying the algorithm.

claim: For smaller particles, running averages that correspond to larger doses may be necessary.
source: For smaller particles, running averages that correspond to larger doses may be necessary, for example 17 electrons/Å2 (seven frames) for the γ-secretase example below and 7 electrons/Å2 (seven frames) for β-galactosidase and complex-I.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the experience gained from applying the algorithm to the test cases.

claim: Overall, Bf and Cf values decrease with higher electron dose, which may be attributed to the relatively faster disappearance of signal at high resolution through radiation damage.
source: Overall, Bf and Cf values decrease with higher electron dose, which may be attributed to the relatively faster disappearance of signal at high resolution through radiation damage.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2 and represents an inference about the cause of the observed trend.

claim: Consistently low values for Bf are observed for the first few movie frames.
source: Interestingly, however, consistently low values for Bf are also observed for the first few movie frames.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2 showing the Bf values for early frames.

claim: During the initial stages of sample irradiation, relatively large beam-induced movements occur.
source: This is in agreement with observations made by others (Brilot et al., 2012; Campbell et al., 2012; Li et al., 2013; Russo and Passmore, 2014; Vinothkumar et al., 2014a) that during the initial stages of sample irradiation relatively large beam-induced movements occur, while sample movement slows down at higher electron doses.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Sample movement slows down at higher electron doses.
source: This is in agreement with observations made by others (Brilot et al., 2012; Campbell et al., 2012; Li et al., 2013; Russo and Passmore, 2014; Vinothkumar et al., 2014a) that during the initial stages of sample irradiation relatively large beam-induced movements occur, while sample movement slows down at higher electron doses.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Electron diffraction spots at 3 Å resolution from bacteriorhodopsin crystals lose 99% of their intensity after a dose of only 3 electrons/Å2.
source: Given that electron diffraction spots at 3 Å resolution from bacteriorhodopsin crystals lose 99% of their intensity after a dose of only 3 electrons/Å2 (Stark et al., 1996), the initial sample movement is extremely detrimental to high-resolution structure determination.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Stark et al., 1996.

claim: The initial sample movement is extremely detrimental to high-resolution structure determination.
source: Given that electron diffraction spots at 3 Å resolution from bacteriorhodopsin crystals lose 99% of their intensity after a dose of only 3 electrons/Å2 (Stark et al., 1996), the initial sample movement is extremely detrimental to high-resolution structure determination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combination of rapid radiation damage and initial movement.

claim: Stopping the initial movement altogether would be a very powerful way to further increase resolution.
source: Therefore, stopping the initial movement altogether would be a very powerful way to further increase resolution, but this has not yet been achieved with existing sample preparation or imaging techniques.
evidence: This is speculation about a potential future improvement.

claim: Stopping the initial movement has not yet been achieved with existing sample preparation or imaging techniques.
source: Therefore, stopping the initial movement altogether would be a very powerful way to further increase resolution, but this has not yet been achieved with existing sample preparation or imaging techniques.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field.

claim: The movie processing algorithm down-weights the high-frequency contributions of the first few movie frames as well as those of the later, high-dose frames.
source: Instead, the movie processing algorithm proposed here down-weights the high-frequency contributions of the first few movie frames, as well as those of the later, high-dose frames.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2 showing the frequency-dependent weights.

claim: Down-weighting early and late frames represents an attractive alternative to merely omitting such frames.
source: This represents an attractive alternative to merely omitting such frames (e.g., see Liao et al., 2013 and Allegretti et al., 2014), since these frames may still contribute useful information to the reconstruction process, particularly at low resolution.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantages of the weighting approach, with citations to alternative approaches.

claim: Early and late frames may still contribute useful information to the reconstruction process, particularly at low resolution.
source: This represents an attractive alternative to merely omitting such frames (e.g., see Liao et al., 2013 and Allegretti et al., 2014), since these frames may still contribute useful information to the reconstruction process, particularly at low resolution.
evidence: This is an inference based on the frequency-dependent weighting scheme shown in Figure 2.

claim: For all four data sets, the reconstructed density is significantly improved by the new movie processing approach.
source: For all four data sets the reconstructed density is significantly improved, thus allowing identification of finer biologically relevant details like separated β-strands or RNA bases in the maps.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3 and Table 1 showing resolution improvements.

claim: The new approach allows identification of finer biologically relevant details like separated β-strands or RNA bases in the maps.
source: For all four data sets the reconstructed density is significantly improved, thus allowing identification of finer biologically relevant details like separated β-strands or RNA bases in the maps.
evidence: This is demonstrated visually in Figure 3 showing improved density maps.

claim: The new approach outperforms the original one for the three smaller complexes.
source: The new approach outperforms the original one for the three smaller complexes.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Table 1 showing better resolution for γ-secretase, β-galactosidase, and complex-I.

claim: For the mitoribosome LSU, the new approach yields a map with 0.05 Å lower resolution than the original approach.
source: Only for the mitoribosome LSU, does the new approach yield a map with 0.05 Å lower resolution than the original approach, although this difference is hard to appreciate in the maps (see Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Table 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: For particles of several megadaltons in size, the determination of rotations and translations is accurate enough to follow particle rotations during the movies.
source: Probably, for particles of several megadaltons in size, the determination of rotations and translations is (just about) accurate enough to follow particle rotations during the movies (also see Brilot et al., 2012 and Campbell et al., 2012), and the omission of rotational searches in the new approach may actually affect the results to a small extent.
evidence: This is speculation based on the results and citations to previous work.

claim: The omission of rotational searches in the new approach may affect the results to a small extent for very large particles.
source: Probably, for particles of several megadaltons in size, the determination of rotations and translations is (just about) accurate enough to follow particle rotations during the movies (also see Brilot et al., 2012 and Campbell et al., 2012), and the omission of rotational searches in the new approach may actually affect the results to a small extent.
evidence: This is speculation based on the slightly lower resolution obtained for the mitoribosome.

claim: For small particles, the accuracy with which particles may be aligned is the limiting factor.
source: (For small particles the accuracy with which such particles may be aligned is the limiting factor, and omitting rotational searches in the movie refinement will probably not have a noticeable effect.)
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the new approach works well for small particles.

claim: Omitting rotational searches in the movie refinement will probably not have a noticeable effect for small particles.
source: (For small particles the accuracy with which such particles may be aligned is the limiting factor, and omitting rotational searches in the movie refinement will probably not have a noticeable effect.)
evidence: This is speculation based on the understanding of alignment limitations for small particles.

claim: The new approach provides a significant speed-up compared to the original approach (a factor of 6 for the mitoribosome data set).
source: Nevertheless, when weighed against the significant speed-up obtained by omitting the rotational searches from the original movie processing approach (a factor of 6 for the mitoribosome data set), even for large particles the new approach may still be preferred over the original one.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Table 1 showing CPU time comparisons.

claim: Even for large particles, the new approach may still be preferred over the original one due to the speed-up.
source: Nevertheless, when weighed against the significant speed-up obtained by omitting the rotational searches from the original movie processing approach (a factor of 6 for the mitoribosome data set), even for large particles the new approach may still be preferred over the original one.
evidence: This is an inference based on the trade-off between speed and marginal resolution difference.

claim: The major advance of the new movie processing approach lies in its applicability to smaller particles.
source: However, the major advance of the new movie processing approach lies in its applicability to smaller particles.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the results for γ-secretase, β-galactosidase, and complex-I in Table 1.

claim: The new approach brings resolutions at which β-strands become separated within reach for particles smaller than 200 kDa.
source: Whereas the original approach was limited to large particles, the new one yields map improvements for a wide range of particles, now bringing resolutions at which β-strands become separated within reach for particles smaller than 200 kDa.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the γ-secretase example (170 kDa) achieving 4.5 Å resolution with visible β-strands in Figure 3.
